title: Hotel search and checkout UI
idea: The hotel frontend is a search page and a checkout flow driven by one reducer that ignores stale searches, repeat clicks and late events.
points: A search id per date change lets the reducer drop answers to older searches.
The reducer owns the hold and payment keys; retries reuse them, so nothing doubles.
A 409 removes the sold-out room type and keeps the guest on the results.
Follow-ups: cache availability by date range, add multi-room carts, and offer price alerts.

edges.label: owns
edges.caption: HotelPage owns the reducer state and passes it down. Children keep no copy of it.

edges.label: search
edges.caption: Each date change bumps the search id and calls GET /availability. Older answers are dropped.
RoomResults shows a card per room type, or a loading or empty state.

edges.label: hold
edges.caption: Choosing a room moves the step to HOLDING. An effect sends POST /reservations with the hold key.
After HOLD_OK the page shows CheckoutPanel and the server's hold deadline.
When the timer hits zero it dispatches HOLD_EXPIRED, unless payment is already in flight.

edges.label: confirm
edges.caption: Pay calls the confirm endpoint with its own key. A timeout retries with the same key.
CONFIRMED moves the page to ConfirmationPage with the reservation id.

code.title: Booking reducer
code.caption: Pure screen logic. Run it, then add a second PAY_CLICKED in a row and predict the output.

walk.text: The whole screen state: step, search id, results, chosen type, two keys and an error.
Each date change starts a new search id; answers for an old id are ignored.
Choosing works only on RESULTS; the same room type keeps its hold key.
A failure keeps the key for a safe retry; a 409 drops the sold-out type.
Pay is ignored unless PAYING; a payment timeout returns to PAYING with the same key.
Hold expiry resets the screen, unless the booking is done or being confirmed.

code.title: RoomResults component
code.caption: A React component that renders state and dispatches events. Not run here.

walk.text: When the step becomes HOLDING, an effect sends the hold with the reducer's key.
Loading and empty states render text, never a blank list.
Errors render in an alert region so screen readers announce them.
Cards disable while a hold is in flight; clicks only dispatch events.

pitfalls: Do not trust response order; a slow old search can overwrite newer results.
Show the server's hold deadline, not a local 15-minute guess; device clocks drift.
Interview follow-up: caching availability means stale counts, so the hold must still recheck.

quiz.q: In the run, what does the stale RESULTS line show as the step?
quiz.why: Two date changes made the current search id 2. The answer for id 1 is ignored, so the step stays SEARCHING.

takeaway: One reducer guards search order, clicks and keys; components only render.

starters: Why keep the hold key when the reserve request fails?
Should I cancel the old fetch with AbortController instead of a search id?
How would I show live availability without polling every few seconds?
